findings.comment: All clearance annotations must be revised to show dimension lines originating at the surveyed outside conductor location (not pole center), with clear identification of which conductor is being measured from, and dimension values showing clearances in feet and inches from the conductor to site features.
applicableAreas: All proposed site features and infrastructure
findings.observation: Complete review of Sheets 9 (Site Plan), 11 (Grading Plan), and 21 (Electrical Plan) reveals NO dimension annotations showing clearances from buildings, structures, driveways, walls, or other site features to overhead electric lines. The only distances shown are from property lines and internal site features to each other. Sheet 4 shows the existing utility poles with symbols but no dimension annotations from the poles. No dimension lines on any sheet are shown extending from an identified 'outside conductor' location to site features. Applicant has not labeled the location of outside conductors or the measurement reference point for any clearance annotations.
findings.reasoning: All clearance dimensions (or lack thereof) must be measured from the outside conductor, not from pole center or pole structure. No clearance dimensions are provided on the plans at all, and no plans identify the location of the outside conductor for measurement purposes.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on site plans, measured from outside conductor as required. All clearance dimensions must originate from the actual conductor location, with notation showing measurement source.
applicableAreas: All locations with clearance dimensions shown on overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the OHE line on the southern boundary of the site but includes NO dimension callouts or clearance annotations of any kind. Wherever clearance dimensions should appear (from conductor to buildings, parking, driveways), none are provided. The few dimension lines visible on Sheet 9 relate to building setbacks and site distances, not to overhead line clearances. The critical requirement to show dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location (not pole centerline) is therefore not met—because no dimensions are shown at all.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires clearance dimensions to be measured from the outside conductor, never from the utility pole centerline. On multi-conductor installations, the conductor may be several feet offset from pole center, creating significant measurement errors if pole-based dimensions are used. The applicant has not provided any clearance dimensions from any overhead electric infrastructure. This is a foundational deficiency—without dimension callouts originating from the conductor, the plans cannot communicate or verify clearance compliance.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions are not shown on any plan sheets. When clearance dimensions are eventually provided, they must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from the utility pole centerline. Dimension lines should clearly identify the conductor location and show measurement to the building edge or feature being evaluated.
applicableAreas: All clearance dimension annotations on site plan
findings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows multiple utility poles and overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) on the property. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows the overhead electric line (OHE) running along the Valley View Road frontage. However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on the plans. The grouping documentation emphasizes that 'All clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), never from the utility pole centerline or pole structure' and warns that 'Measuring from pole centerline instead of the conductor results in understated clearances and code violations.' Since no dimensions are shown on the plans at all, there is no evidence that the applicant is measuring from the outside conductor versus the pole.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Measurement Methodology section: 'Profile plans must show dimension lines originating at the conductor location, not at the pole. [This is critical.]' The complete absence of clearance dimensions means there is no opportunity to verify that dimensions originate from the conductor rather than the pole. This is a fundamental documentation failure that prevents verification of compliance. Without at least one dimension showing the measurement methodology and origin point (outside conductor), compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Electrical conduit branch lines route directly to electrical meters mounted on the exterior walls of all 8 buildings. No dimensional callouts on the electrical plan verify that the required 5-foot horizontal clearance from building foundations to underground electric facilities is maintained at meter connection locations. Provide detailed electrical design or utility coordination drawings showing the routing of electrical branch lines and confirming minimum 5-foot clearance from building foundations, or provide documentation of an approved variance/coordination with Austin Energy if reduced clearances have been authorized.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters mounted on the exterior walls of all 8 buildings (Buildings 1-8). Branch conduit lines must route from the main underground electrical trunk lines to these wall-mounted meters. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that electrical routing approaches and connects directly to these meters on the building exteriors, with the branch lines definitely entering the area within 5 feet of building foundations at all meter connection locations. No dimensional callouts on the electrical plan verify that the 5-foot horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to building foundations is maintained at any of these meter connection points.
findings.reasoning: Building foundations must maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (duct banks, conduit, pull boxes) per UCM § 1.10.5.B. The electrical meters mounted directly on the exterior walls at each building require electrical service lines to run to those wall locations. The vision tool analysis explicitly noted that electrical routing enters the <5-foot zone at all eight meter connection locations. Without explicit dimensional documentation on the plans showing the 5-foot clearance is maintained, and given the physical requirement for conduit to reach wall-mounted meters, the minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified as met.

findings.comment: All eight building foundations have underground electric conduit routing within 5 feet (typically within 0 to 2 feet) of building walls to serve wall-mounted electrical meters. This violates the required 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to building foundations. Either relocate meters to comply with clearance or coordinate with Austin Energy for exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B.
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, scale 1" = 20') reveals that electrical meters are mounted directly on the building foundation walls for all eight buildings. Underground electric conduit and lines routing to these meters are shown running immediately adjacent to (and in some cases directly against) the building foundation walls. Specifically: Building 1 meter on northwest corner wall with conduit running along west foundation; Building 2 meter on south wall with branch line routing directly to recessed area; Building 3 meter on east wall with line running to foundation; Building 4 meter on north wall with line from northeast pull box; Building 7 meter on east wall with conduit from southeast corner; Building 8 meter on north wall (recessed notch) with lines routing along foundations. The electrical conduit serving each meter breaches the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone and runs within inches of the building foundations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires a minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (duct banks, conduit, pull boxes, manholes) to customer buildings and foundations. The site plan clearly shows electrical meters mounted directly on building walls with underground conduit routed immediately adjacent to building foundations. This is a direct violation of the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. The presence of wall-mounted meters inherently requires conduit to enter the building within the 5-foot zone. This is not a design that coordinates with the clearance requirement—it fundamentally violates it.

findings.comment: Electrical transformer pads are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8, but no horizontal clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from building foundations. Add clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all transformer pads are positioned at least 5 feet from the nearest building structure.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows five electrical transformer pads positioned on the site: west of Building 1 (northwest), southwest of Building 2 (west), east of Building 4 (center/east), east of Building 6 (east), and west of Building 8 (southwest). The transformer locations are clearly labeled with callout boxes and rectangular symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building footprints and overall site layout. However, no horizontal clearance dimensions are shown between any of the transformer pads and the building foundations or walls. The plans lack any notation, dimension line, or measurement indicating the distance from transformer pads to the nearest building structure. The Utility Notes on Sheet 21 state that "Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities prior to construction" and "notify engineer of any conflicts/discrepancies prior to installation," but this is a general directive rather than a demonstration that the 5-foot minimum clearance has been verified and documented on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that building foundations maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (including transformer pads). The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through the site plan documentation. Presence of transformer pads on the plan combined with absence of clearance verification constitutes missing required information. The transformer locations are shown but no evidence is provided that they maintain the required 5-foot separation from buildings. Without dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or specific distance notations on the plans, it cannot be confirmed that this requirement has been addressed. The general contractor verification note is inadequate as a substitute for plan-based documentation of compliance.

findings.comment: Electrical plan shows 8 pull box locations but does not document that each pull box is located inside the property line and maintains 5-foot clearance from all sides. Provide dimensional callouts or a coordination note verifying all pull box locations meet the property line and clearance requirements, or revise pull box locations if necessary to comply.
applicableAreas: Pull box locations throughout site perimeter and interior
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows 8 electrical pull boxes labeled and located at various positions around the site: north of Building 1, west of Building 2, west of Building 8, south of Building 7, southeast of Building 7/southwest of Building 6, east of Building 4, northeast of Building 3, and north of Building 5. However, the electrical plan contains no dimensional callouts or annotations verifying that each pull box is (1) located inside the property line and (2) maintains 5 feet clearance from all sides of the pull box structure. The plan does not explicitly confirm these clearance requirements are met.
findings.reasoning: Pull boxes must be located inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides per UCM § 1.10.5.B. While the pull boxes are shown on the electrical plan, there is no documentation verifying these requirements are met. The pull boxes appear to be located at various positions relative to property lines and site features, but without dimensional callouts or notes confirming the clearances, compliance cannot be verified from the plans.

findings.comment: Four electrical pull boxes (near Buildings 1, 4, 7, and 8) are positioned within 5 feet of building foundations and corners. Relocate pull boxes to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all sides per UCM § 1.10.5.B, or provide justification if clearance maintenance is infeasible and coordinate with Austin Energy Design.
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) reveals electrical pull boxes positioned in close proximity to building foundations at multiple locations: (1) Building 1: Pull box at southwest corner, appearing to be within 5 feet (visually estimated 2-4 feet) of the corner; (2) Building 4: Pull box to the northeast near Unit 404, positioned close to the east foundation line, appearing to be at or near the 5-foot threshold; (3) Building 7: Pull box at southeast corner near Unit 704, appearing to be within 5 feet of the corner; (4) Building 8: Pull box at northwest corner near Unit 801, appearing to be within 5 feet of the corner. These pull boxes are shown as discrete symbols positioned immediately adjacent to building corners rather than at clear standoff distances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires pull boxes to maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides, including from building foundations and property lines. Pull boxes are underground electrical facilities that must be accessible for maintenance, and the code establishes clearance from structures to ensure they are not impacted by building foundations or other improvements. The visual positioning of pull boxes at or within building corners (at the 1" = 20' scale) indicates they fail to maintain the required 5-foot clearance zone around them. This is particularly problematic because pull boxes require working space for access and maintenance.

findings.comment: Electrical pull boxes are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan in eight locations around the site perimeter, but no clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they are located inside the property line and maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from all sides. Add clearance dimensions or notes to the electrical plan confirming each pull box location complies with the minimum distance requirements.
applicableAreas: Electrical pull box locations distributed throughout site perimeter
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly identifies eight electrical pull box locations distributed around the site perimeter using callout boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' with leader lines pointing to small nodes on the blue underground electric lines. Pull boxes are positioned: near the transformer pad west of Building 1, south of Building 2, west of Building 8, north of Building 3, east of Building 5, east of Building 6, and south of Building 7. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or written notes indicating the horizontal distance of these pull boxes from property lines or from adjacent site features (buildings, walls, driveways, etc.). Specifically, no documentation is provided showing that pull boxes are inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides as required.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that pull boxes be located inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides. The location of pull boxes on the plan is noted, but the specific clearance requirements are not documented. Without dimension callouts or verification notes showing that each pull box is inside the property line and maintains the required 5-foot separation, compliance cannot be confirmed. The absence of this required information on the plans constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: The proposed electrical design shows one meter per building serving multiple units, not separate meters and service drops for each individual townhome unit as required by UCM § 1.3.8. Revise the electrical design to provide individual service drops and separate electrical meters for each of the 39 individual townhome units. Coordinate with Austin Energy Design to confirm the individual unit metering requirements and service configuration for this multi-unit townhome development.
applicableAreas: All 39 individual townhome units across 8 buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight (8) locations labeled 'Electrical Meters' with one meter assigned to each building: Building 1 (north wall), Building 2 (west wall), Building 3 (north wall), Building 4 (north wall), Building 5 (east wall), Building 6 (west wall), Building 7 (south wall), and Building 8 (north wall). The site plan describes 39 total townhome units distributed across these 8 buildings, with buildings varying in size from 3,290 sf to 4,997 sf. Based on square footage and typical townhome unit sizes (approximately 1,000-1,400 sf per unit), each building contains approximately 3-5 units. The design provides one electrical meter per building (building-level service), not one meter per individual residential unit.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.8 requires that 'Each individual unit [shall have a] separate service drop and meter as required by AE standards.' The cited code section addresses customer electrical facilities and specifically contemplates individual unit service. In multi-unit residential development (such as townhomes), Austin Energy standards typically require individual unit metering to allow for separate billing, service control, and load management per residential unit. The proposed design with one meter per building serving 3-5 units per building does not provide the required individual unit service drops and meters. A building with 5 units served by one meter lacks the four additional required service drops and meters that UCM § 1.3.8 requires.

findings.comment: Provide documentation from Austin Energy Design confirming that each of the 39 townhome units has a separate service drop and individual meter as required by AE standards per UCM § 1.3.8. Include service drop routing details and AE approval correspondence.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 buildings with individual unit meters (gang meters) for 39 townhome units. Vision analysis confirmed: 'There are eight (8) specific callouts reading..."Electrical Meters." There is one callout pointing to an exterior wall of every single building (Bldgs. 1 through 8)...visual hash marks on those banks roughly correspond to the number of units in that specific building, these appear to be clustered individual unit meters (gang meters).' However, no documentation found indicating: (1) how many individual service drops are provided per unit, (2) whether each unit has its own service drop from the transformer pad, (3) AE approval of individual unit meter configuration for townhome units per AE standards, or (4) whether the design meets AE requirements for individual unit service in multi-unit developments.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Each individual unit lacking separate service drop and meter as required by AE standards' per UCM § 1.3.8. While gang meters are shown, AE requires separate service drops for each unit in multi-unit residential developments. The preliminary design shows meters clustered by building but does not document how many service drops are provided or whether AE Design approved individual service drops per unit. Without AE Design approval confirming each unit has a separate service drop and meter per AE standards, this cannot be confirmed as compliant.

findings.comment: Individual unit service configuration unclear. Design shows 8 meter locations for 39 units, but whether each unit has individual service drop and meter per Austin Energy standards is not documented. Unified development determination not visible.
findings.observation: The project proposes 39 multi-family townhome units across 8 buildings. Sheet 21 shows electrical meters labeled for 8 locations (one per building). Sheet 29 is the Addressing Plan showing individual unit addresses, suggesting each unit has a separate address. However, the preliminary electrical design shows 8 meter locations for 39 units, implying not every individual unit has a separate meter. The requirement for each unit to have separate service drop and meter per AE standards is unclear without detailed electrical specifications or Austin Energy approval documentation.
findings.reasoning: For multi-unit developments like townhomes, Austin Energy standard practice typically requires separate service drops and meters for each individual unit (unless the development qualifies for consolidated service under unified development provisions). The preliminary design shows 8 meters for 39 units, suggesting shared/consolidated service. Without documentation confirming either: (1) Austin Energy approval for consolidated/shared service across multiple units, or (2) individual meters for each unit, this requirement cannot be verified as met. The grouping's Regulatory Overview notes that unified development status 'cannot be determined from plans alone—requires Austin Energy determination based on ownership, development pattern, and operational characteristics.'

findings.comment: Proposed electrical routing path from existing service to proposed buildings shown with blue line on Sheet 21, but route lacks dimensional callouts, measurements, turning points, depth changes, and routing specifications necessary for Austin Energy approval. Add detailed routing callouts with dimensions, clear identification of route path segments, and transition point specifications.
applicableAreas: West property line from existing service connection to all proposed service points
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed electrical route as a blue line originating from existing underground electric line on west side near Valley View Road, connecting to a pull box, then to transformer pads and building service locations. However, the routing lacks explicit dimensioning and callout notations showing the exact path, transition points, depth changes, and equipment relationships. No measurements, distances, or routing specifications are provided beyond the visual line representation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires the proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service to be explicitly shown on plans. While a routing path is visible, complete documentation requires measurements, directional callouts, depth specifications, turning points, and clearance details to enable Austin Energy review and construction verification. A visual blue line without dimensional documentation is insufficient for design approval.

findings.comment: Proposed electrical service route from existing Austin Energy connection to proposed service points is not clearly documented. Please provide: (1) one-line electrical schematic showing service path from AE connection point to each building's service entrance; (2) annotations on site plan showing service routing with arrows and labels; (3) notes identifying which route serves which building; (4) identification of any intermediate disconnect/metering locations.
applicableAreas: From point of connection through entire service routing to all buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows blue conduit lines routing throughout the site, but the routing path from the point of connection (which itself is not clearly identified per EL-10.14 finding) to the proposed service point(s)/buildings is not clearly labeled or documented. While conduit lines are drawn, there are no notes, annotations, or callouts explaining the routing path, voltage being carried, or service endpoint. No schematic or one-line diagram shows the electrical service path from AE system to each building.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service [to be] shown.' The current plans show conduit routing graphically but lack the documentation needed to understand: (1) which route serves which building, (2) whether service enters from front or rear, (3) intermediate connection points, (4) service voltage and load at each endpoint. This documentation is essential for demonstrating that the routing complies with AE requirements (e.g., 20-foot maximum meter-to-disconnect distance, meter accessibility, etc.).

findings.comment: Proposed electrical service routing from existing Austin Energy infrastructure to proposed service not shown. Clearly show the routing path for the service entrance, including conduit sizing, length, and routing details from the point of connection to the proposed transformer locations.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines (blue solid lines with callout box labeled 'Underground Electric Line') connecting transformers and pull boxes to building meter locations. However, the vision analysis confirms that while these lines show internal site routing between proposed equipment, there is no indication of how the service enters the site or connects from the existing AE facilities at the property boundary to the proposed transformers and meters. The plan shows internal site electric routing but does not trace the service path from the point where it would connect to existing AE infrastructure (shown as 'OHE' lines and poles near property boundaries) to the proposed transformer pads and distribution points on the site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown' and specifically requires documentation of 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service.' This requirement ensures that the applicant has coordinated with AE regarding the service entrance location, the routing path, and any required conduit or ductwork. Without this routing shown, it is unclear whether the service can physically reach the proposed transformer locations, whether it conflicts with site improvements, or whether adequate space and clearances exist. The absence of service routing from existing to proposed facilities prevents verification of the overall service design completeness.

findings.comment: Number of 90-degree turns in electrical routing from each transformer to meter not documented. Provide detailed electrical routing schedule or plan annotations showing the count of 90-degree bends in the conduit path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter(s), confirming maximum two 90-degree bends.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths from transformers to meters on all eight buildings
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) which shows electrical routing from transformers to meters. Blue lines represent underground electric lines routed from transformers through pull boxes to meters on buildings. Visual inspection of the routing paths shows multiple turns. For example, routing from the transformer pad adjacent to Building 8 to the building's meters shows approximately 2 turn angles. However, the plan is schematic and does not explicitly count or label the number of 90-degree bends at each turn location. For many routing paths, multiple 90-degree turns are visually apparent as the lines navigate around building footprints and follow driveway layouts, but exact turn counts are not documented.
findings.reasoning: Code requires maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer and meter. While the electrical routing shows various path configurations, the plan does not explicitly document or count the number of 90-degree bends in each routing path. Without precise notation of turn counts, it is unclear whether any routing exceeds the maximum of two 90-degree turns. Some routing paths appear to have more than two distinct directional changes. The schematic nature of the plan makes definitive turn counting difficult without detailed field verification or explicit turn counts on the design.

findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 contains at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary underground electrical loop, exceeding the maximum of 2 turns permitted by UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q. The rectangular loop configuration around the central buildings necessitates multiple directional changes. Revise the electrical routing design to limit turns between transformer pads and meters to a maximum of two 90-degree bends, or provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing the exceeding the standard 2-turn limitation for this site configuration.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing path from transformers to meters throughout site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 to trace electrical routing paths and count 90-degree bends. Vision analysis traced 'the primary electrical routing is denoted by a solid blue line. It enters the site from the mid-western boundary... splits to form a continuous underground loop that follows the inner perimeter of the internal drive aisle, circling the central buildings.' The analysis specifically identified: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends. Counting just the primary main loop (excluding small jogs to individual pads/meters), there are at least 6 distinct 90-degree corners to navigate the rectangular layout of the site.' The primary electrical loop makes a rectangular circuit around the central buildings, requiring approximately 6 90-degree directional changes (one at each corner of the rectangular loop). Branch connections from this main loop to individual transformers and meters add additional turns.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q (Current Transformers and Enclosures) specifies 'maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter.' This limitation is imposed to maintain circuit performance and prevent voltage drop issues. The vision analysis conclusively identified at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary electrical routing loop, which is triple the maximum allowable. The rectangular main loop circuit requires a 90-degree bend at each corner (north, east, south, west), and the perimeter-following design necessitates these turns. This configuration cannot be reconfigured without a complete redesign of the electrical routing topology. The current design violates the maximum two-turn requirement.

findings.comment: More than two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter. Most routing paths show multiple bends to navigate around building perimeters.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan, scale 1" = 20') vision analysis identified the electrical routing pattern: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends throughout the site\'s electrical routing. Almost every path from a transformer to a distant meter (e.g., from the west pad to Bldg 3, or from the east pads to Bldg 5 and 7) involves multiple 90-degree turns to navigate around building corners and pull boxes.' The vision analysis did not identify a single routing path with two or fewer 90-degree bends; instead, it confirmed that most paths have 'multiple' (three or more) bends.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q limits electrical routing between transformer and meter to a maximum of two 90-degree bends. The site layout with buildings positioned around the central parking loop necessitates multiple turns to reach distant meter locations. Vision analysis explicitly confirmed 'numerous 90-degree bends' on most routing paths, with specific mention that paths to Buildings 3, 5, and 7 involve 'multiple 90-degree turns.' This pattern demonstrates systematic non-compliance across multiple meter routing paths.

findings.comment: Electrical meters are scattered across multiple building locations throughout the site rather than grouped at a common location. Meters shown on Bldg. 1, Bldg. 2, Bldg. 5, Bldg. 8 areas, and spaces between buildings - separated by 60+ feet, exceeding the 20-foot maximum. No disconnects are shown on the plan. Applicant must group all meters and disconnects at a common location within 20 feet separation and line of sight.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters distributed across multiple locations throughout the site, with meters located adjacent to different buildings: north side of Bldg. 1/3, space between Bldg. 2 and Bldg. 4, east side of Bldg. 5, west side of Bldg. 8, and space between Bldg. 6 and Bldg. 7. This represents at least 5-6 separate meter locations spread across the entire site rather than grouped in one common location. The plan does not label or depict any disconnect switches or show grouping of meters and disconnects at a single location. No disconnects are explicitly shown anywhere on the sheet. The scale is 1" = 20', which means the distances between these scattered meter locations would be approximately 60-100+ feet apart based on the spatial distribution visible in the drawing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and line of sight. The site plan shows meters scattered across multiple buildings throughout the 2.16-acre site - a configuration that cannot comply with the 20-foot maximum distance requirement. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that meters and disconnects are grouped at a common location or that the 20-foot maximum separation is met. The absence of any labeled disconnects on the electrical design sheet, combined with the scattered meter locations, constitutes non-compliance with the grouping and distance requirements.

findings.comment: Meters and disconnects not grouped together with documented separation distance. Identify and label all electrical disconnects on the site plan. Show distance measurements between meters and disconnects, documenting that separation does not exceed 20 feet and that meters and disconnects are within line of sight. Verify grouping in common location per UCM § 1.9.3.1(I).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows 'Electrical Meters' labeled on the exteriors of the eight buildings (noted near units 102/103, 201/202, 301/302, 401/402, 501/502, 603, 701/702, 801/802). However, 'Electrical Disconnects' are NOT explicitly labeled or identified anywhere on the sheet. No dimension lines or distance measurements are shown between the meter locations and any disconnect locations. No distance verification is possible to confirm meters and disconnects are grouped together or that separation does not exceed the 20-foot maximum. Pull boxes are shown but cannot be confirmed as disconnects.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and within line of sight. Sheet 21 shows meters but does not identify disconnects as distinct labeled elements. Without both meters and disconnects identified and dimensioned, compliance with the grouping, separation distance, and line-of-sight requirements cannot be verified. The applicant has not provided sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance.

findings.comment: Meters and transformers are not grouped in a common location and are separated by more than 20 feet in multiple instances, exceeding the maximum separation allowed. Some meter/transformer pairs may lack adequate line of sight. Reconfigure electrical infrastructure to group meters and disconnects in common locations within 20 feet of each transformer, with clear line of sight maintained between all paired equipment.
applicableAreas: Transformers 1, 2, and 3 locations; building meter locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three electrical transformer pads and six meter locations (on building exteriors). Vision analysis measured separation distances between transformer pads and associated meter banks: Transformer 1 to meters range 30-50 feet; Transformer 2 to meters range 10-150 feet; Transformer 3 to meters range 60-150 feet. The transformers are located in standalone pads in easements/common areas, while meters are mounted on building walls. These two types of equipment are not grouped together in common locations. Some meter/transformer pairs may have line-of-sight obstructions created by building corners.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires meters and disconnects to be grouped together in a common location, with maximum 20-foot separation, and within line of sight of each other. The separation distances measured on the electrical plan exceed the 20-foot maximum threshold for multiple transformer/meter combinations. Additionally, transformers and meters are not grouped in a common location but are dispersed across the site (transformers in separate pads; meters on individual building exteriors). The requirement for line of sight is potentially not met where building structures create obstructions between transformer pads and associated meters.

findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on the plans traverses the site to connect to building-mounted meters and runs through internal site corridors. Although the primary trunk lines may route around the building perimeter, no explicit documentation verifies that no underground electric facilities pass beneath the footprints of any of the 8 buildings, nor are any Austin Energy coordination agreements or exceptions noted on the plans. Provide a certified site plan overlay or coordination letter from Austin Energy confirming that no underground electric facilities pass under any building foundations, or revise electrical routing if conflicts exist.
applicableAreas: Building footprints relative to underground electric routing
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the footprints of all 8 buildings. Sheets 19 (Utility Tap Plan) and 21 (Electrical Design Plan) show proposed electric line routing throughout the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted that 'The routing is indicated by solid blue lines originating from a connection labeled Underground Electric Line on the western property boundary' and that 'The main trunk lines route primarily around the outer perimeter of the development rather than crossing under the building foundations.' However, the electrical plan also shows branch lines extending from the main trunk to connect to meters on each building, and internal routing that passes between buildings. While the vision analysis suggested main lines route around the perimeter, no explicit documentation was found verifying that no electric facilities pass under any building foundations, nor were any exceptions or coordination agreements noted on the plans.
findings.reasoning: Customer buildings and permanent structures shall not be installed over Austin Energy underground facilities per UCM § 1.10.5.B. The electrical routing shown on Sheets 19 and 21 demonstrates that electric lines do traverse the site. While the primary trunk lines may route around the building perimeter, branch lines must connect to meters and the overall routing passes through the site where buildings are located. Without explicit documentation verifying that no electric facilities pass beneath any building foundations, and without any noted exceptions or coordination agreements with Austin Energy, compliance with this prohibition cannot be confirmed. The vision analysis suggested routing avoids direct conflicts, but this is not the same as documented verification.

findings.comment: Underground electric conduit routing to serve wall-mounted electrical meters on all eight buildings would require conduit to pass beneath or through building foundations, which violates UCM § 1.10.5.B. Relocate electrical meters to pedestals or external equipment enclosures outside of building footprints, or coordinate with Austin Energy Design to document a license agreement and sealed engineering design if conduit must pass through building foundations, with metal sleeves allowing replacement.
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows that underground electric conduit is routed to and directly beneath building foundations to serve electrical meters mounted on building walls. Specifically: (1) All eight buildings have underground electric lines routing to wall-mounted meters; (2) These lines originate from transformers or pull boxes and run directly to the building serving as conduit entry points; (3) The conduit must pass beneath or immediately adjacent to building foundations to reach the meters; (4) In some cases (Buildings 2, 8), the meters are mounted in recessed notches in the building walls, requiring conduit to route into these recessed areas. This represents a direct routing of underground electric facilities beneath building foundations and service areas.
findings.reasoning: Wall-mounted electrical meters inherently require underground conduit to be routed to the building. When buildings are designed with slab-on-grade construction (as noted in the site data), conduit routing beneath the slab violates the prohibition. While some conduit may pass through retaining walls below grade (with an exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B requiring license agreement and engineering), the routing of conduit as the primary service to wall-mounted meters is not addressed by this exception.

findings.comment: Obtain approval from AE Metering Group for all meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3. Verify each meter is: (1) outdoors, (2) readily accessible, (3) on first floor/ground level, (4) within sight of the AE transformer, and (5) not in prohibited locations (under porches, under overhangs >72 inches, within 3-foot radius of gas meters). Provide detailed meter location plans and AE approval correspondence.
applicableAreas: Eight building locations - individual unit meter locations shown on Sheet 21
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows eight individual 'Electrical Meters' callouts (one for each building). Vision analysis indicated these appear to be individual unit meters (gang meters). However, no documentation found indicating meter locations were discussed with or approved by AE Metering Group. UCM § 1.9.3 requires meters be: (1) outdoors, (2) readily accessible, (3) on first floor/ground level, (4) within sight of AE transformer. No details provided on Sheet 21 showing that these meter locations meet these requirements. No approval correspondence from AE Metering Group located.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'Meter locations not approved by AE Metering Group per UCM § 1.9.3.' While meters are shown on Sheet 21, no evidence was found that: (1) AE Metering Group reviewed and approved these locations, or (2) the meter locations comply with UCM § 1.9.3 requirements (outdoor, accessible, first floor, within sight of transformer). For a multi-unit development, individual unit meters need specific AE approval of locations. This is a deficiency.

findings.comment: Meter locations shown on preliminary design but approval from Austin Energy Metering Group not documented. No correspondence or approval evidence from AE Metering Group (Distribution Metering) visible in accessible documentation.
applicableAreas: Sheet 21 - 8 meter locations on building exteriors
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations (one per building) labeled as 'Electrical Meters' attached to building exteriors: Bldg. 1 north wall, Bldg. 2 south wall, Bldg. 3 north wall, Bldg. 4 north wall, Bldg. 5 north wall, Bldg. 6 south wall, Bldg. 7 south wall, Bldg. 8 south wall. However, the preliminary design does not show: meter specifications, enclosure types, accessibility details, or approval from Austin Energy's Metering Group. No correspondence approving meter locations is visible in accessible documentation.
findings.reasoning: The requirement states 'Meter locations [must be] approved by AE Metering Group per UCM § 1.9.3.' While meter locations are proposed on the preliminary design, approval from Austin Energy's Metering Group (distinct from Austin Energy Design) is not documented. The grouping's Regulatory Overview specifies that 'Written approval from both AE Design and Distribution Metering business unit required for any exceptions.' The preliminary design shows meter locations but provides no evidence of Metering Group approval or compliance documentation.

findings.comment: Clearance dimensions for electric facilities not documented on plans. Add clearance dimensions to the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan showing that all proposed electrical facilities (transformers, conductors, meter pedestals, service lines) maintain required clearances from buildings, drainage features, trees, and other structures per UCM § 1.16.0(2) and National Electric Safety Code standards.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical equipment (transformers, meters, pull boxes) and underground routing but does not include specific clearance dimensions or annotations demonstrating compliance with safety clearance standards. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 provides utility notes about water and wastewater specifications but does not reference electrical clearance dimensions. Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement clearance requirements (noting no digging within 25 feet, no trees within 25 feet, 20-foot clearance for equipment) but the site plan does not dimension these clearances for verification.
findings.reasoning: Plans must demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2). This includes clearances per the National Electric Safety Code and City of Austin requirements. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows the general layout, specific clearance dimensions from buildings, drainage features, trees, and other structures are not annotated on the plan. This makes verification of clearance compliance impossible. Clearance dimensions must be shown on the plans with annotations confirming compliance.

findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate sufficient clearances for electric facilities. Sheet 21 lacks dimensioned clearance information for proposed electric infrastructure. Add clearance dimensions to electrical plans showing: (1) minimum setbacks of transformer pads and pull boxes from buildings per NEC standards, (2) clearances from all drainage features per UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.7, (3) clearances from other utilities, (4) 25-foot clearance from transmission structures, and (5) clearance maintenance areas accessible for Austin Energy.
applicableAreas: Electric facility clearances on site plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground routing with location labels but NO clearance dimensions are shown. Vision analysis confirmed absence of clearance callouts, setback dimensions from buildings, property lines, drainage features, or other infrastructure. The transmission line requirements on Sheet 3 Block 20 specify clearances (25 feet from structures, 20 feet for aerial equipment/staging) but these are notes, not dimensioned on electrical drawings. No clearance schedule or detailed specification table accompanies the electrical design.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires plans demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities per design and safety standards. The preliminary designation of Sheet 21 and complete absence of dimensioned clearances (setbacks, vertical clearances from pond, horizontal separations) fails to meet this requirement. While transmission clearance requirements are listed in notes, the actual proposed site layout does not include clearance dimensions to verify compliance.

findings.comment: Proposed conduit routing shown on Sheet 21, but conduit sizing (pipe diameter, duct bank dimensions, material specifications) not labeled or specified. Complete conduit sizing and material specifications must be added to all electrical routing documentation.
applicableAreas: Underground electrical conduit routing throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed electrical infrastructure including three transformer pads, multiple pull boxes, electrical meters on all eight buildings, and underground conduit routing depicted as blue lines connecting service entry point on west side to all facilities. However, the proposed conduit routing lacks specification of pipe sizing/diameter. Utility Notes on Sheet 21 require contractors to verify existing utilities but do not specify proposed conduit sizes, material, or duct bank dimensions required for design compliance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) requires complete documentation of proposed electric facilities including distribution lines and all infrastructure. Incomplete facility specifications (missing conduit sizes, pipe diameters, duct bank details) constitute incomplete documentation of proposed infrastructure. The blue lines show routing paths but lack the engineering specifications necessary for Austin Energy approval and construction.

findings.comment: Proposed electrical facilities are incompletely shown. Please provide: (1) conduit sizing and material specifications for all underground routing on Sheets 9, 11, 19, and 21; (2) transformer pad kVA ratings and voltage configurations; (3) distribution line sizes; (4) pull box dimensions; (5) consistent depiction of all proposed equipment across all plan sheets (Site Plan, Grading, Utility Tap, and Electrical Plan sheets).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformers (4 pad-mounted), meters (attached to 7 buildings), pull boxes, and underground conduit routing in blue. However, vision analysis identified critical absences: No conduit sizing or material specifications are labeled, no transformer kVA ratings or voltage configurations are shown, no pull box dimensions, no distribution line sizes. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and lacks all underground routing and meters. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows no electric distribution lines at all. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend symbols for 'Proposed Underground Electric' and 'Transformer Pad' but NO actual facilities are drawn on the plan view.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) and (5) require proposed electric facilities to be 'shown' with sufficient detail. While Sheet 21 provides some proposed facilities (transformers, meters, routing), the incompleteness includes: (1) no conduit/wire sizing, (2) no transformer ratings, (3) no voltage designations, (4) no equipment specifications. More critically, cross-sheet inconsistency means critical sheets (9, 11, 19) do not show the complete proposed design shown on Sheet 21, violating the requirement that proposed facilities be shown across applicable plan sheets. The lack of specifications on Sheet 21 and absence on other sheets together constitute incomplete documentation per UCM § 1.16.0(5).

findings.comment: Power source for proposed buildings not clearly identified. Please add: (1) equipment schedule or one-line diagram showing which transformer(s) serve which buildings; (2) service voltage and load data for each building; (3) connection routing from transformers to each building's service entrance; (4) clarification of whether multiple buildings share service or have individual service points.
findings.observation: Examined electrical design plan and site plan for power source indication. Sheet 21 shows 4 proposed transformer pads and meters on buildings but does not identify which transformer(s) serve which buildings. No callouts or connection lines indicate power routing from transformers to specific buildings. No indication of primary vs. secondary service. Sheet 9 shows one transformer pad but no meters and no indication of service routing. The electrical design does not include a one-line diagram, equipment schedule, or notes identifying the power source for the 39 residential units.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Power source for proposed buildings.' The omission of this information means: (1) it is unclear which transformer(s) power which buildings, (2) there is no indication whether multiple buildings share service or each has individual service (violating potential unified development documentation), (3) load distribution among transformers cannot be verified. This is a fundamental requirement for demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.3.3 (one point of service, one service voltage per building).

findings.comment: Proposed power source and service specifications (voltage, amperage, service type) not identified for proposed buildings. Specify the service voltage (primary/secondary), amperage, and service type (single/three-phase) for each building or building group on the electrical design plan.
applicableAreas: Site plan, Electrical design plan - all proposed buildings
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows 8 proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8). Vision analysis confirms that meters are depicted on the buildings with generic 'Electrical Meters' labels, and transformers are shown as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' callouts. However, the plan does not clearly indicate the power source (service voltage, amperage, or service type) for any of the proposed buildings. The vision tool response explicitly states: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.' While the sheet shows where meters and transformers will be located graphically, there is no accompanying text, table, or note identifying the service voltage, service type (primary/secondary), or how each building will be powered.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires that plans show 'Power source for proposed buildings' as part of the application requirements for Austin Energy land development review. The grouping's Regulatory Overview states that 'Point of service identified with one service voltage' must be shown on plans (item #7 under Plan Documentation Requirements). The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms no text or labels indicating service voltage, amperage, or service type for the proposed buildings. While the physical locations of meters and transformers are graphically depicted, without identification of the power source (voltage level and capacity), the requirement to show 'power source for proposed buildings' is not met. This is distinct from EL-10.8 (proposed facilities shown) because the facilities themselves may be shown, but their functional designation as power source is missing.

findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) does not include clearance dimensions between the underground electric lines and buildings, permanent structures, or other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain). Add clearance callouts and dimensions to the electrical site plan, and provide profile or cross-section views where electric lines cross other utilities to demonstrate compliance with applicable clearance standards.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric line routing, transformer pad locations, and meter locations but does not include clearance dimensions between buildings, permanent structures (retaining walls, fences), other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain lines), and the electric facilities. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted 'Because this is a 2D plan view without depths or profile details provided on this sheet, vertical conflicts or clearance issues cannot be definitively assessed, though numerous horizontal crossing points are evident.' Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water, wastewater, and storm drain crossing electric line locations but does not provide clearance dimensions. No profile sheets showing vertical clearances between electric lines and other utilities are evident in the sheet index.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that plans 'demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities.' The requirement is to show 'Clearance dimensions shown for buildings, permanent structures, and other utilities relative to electric facilities.' The absence of clearance callouts and dimensions on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) constitutes non-compliance. At minimum, where underground electric lines cross or run parallel to water, wastewater, and storm drain lines, the clearance dimensions (vertical separation) must be clearly shown. Profile views or cross-sections may be required to demonstrate adequate vertical separation.

findings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to all plan sheets showing sufficient clearances between electrical facilities (transformers, meters, conduit, overhead lines) and buildings, other utilities, and landscaping per UCM § 1.16.0(2). Provide dimensions per UCM § 1.10.3 (overhead clearances) and UCM § 1.10.4 (padmount equipment clearances).
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) for clearance dimensions between electrical facilities and other structures. No dimension callouts or clearance notes are shown between transformer pads and buildings, between overhead electric lines and buildings/structures, between underground conduit and other utilities, or between electrical equipment and landscaping. No clearance specifications per UCM § 1.10.3 (Clearances from AE Overhead Lines) or UCM § 1.10.4 (Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment) are noted on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires plans to demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities. This is critical for safety, maintenance, and code compliance. The absence of clearance dimensions or specifications creates uncertainty about whether electrical facilities meet minimum setback requirements from buildings, other utilities, and landscaping. While the infrastructure is shown, the clearances are not demonstrated through dimensional callouts or specification notes.

findings.comment: Section views showing existing electrical pole heights, all conductor elevations, and required clearance envelopes (minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance) are not provided. Please provide detailed electrical profile/section views showing all existing overhead facilities with heights and clearance demonstrations.
applicableAreas: All elevation/profile views with existing overhead facilities in proximity
findings.observation: Examined available section and elevation sheets. Sheet 21 references 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' but vision analysis of Sheet 19 found NO profile views present—only plan view with notes. No dedicated section views showing heights, conductor spacing, or clearance envelopes were located on Sheet 19. No profile sheets explicitly showing existing electrical pole heights and all conductors were found in the available plan set. While Sheet 3 contains transmission clearance notes, no graphical cross-sections or elevation views demonstrating pole heights and clearance envelopes are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires section views to show 'height of existing electrical poles and all conductors with clearance envelopes.' Although section views exist in the plan set (e.g., storm sewer profiles on other sheets), the electrical profile information referenced on Sheet 21 is not provided. The absence of dedicated electrical section views with pole heights, conductor elevations, and clearance envelopes (typically 7.5 feet horizontal minimum clearance per UCM § 1.10.3) means the clearance compliance cannot be verified graphically.

findings.comment: Underground electric cable and conduit clearances from buildings, foundations, and permanent structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details on utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from all AE underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Underground electric conduit routing throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (marked as blue solid lines with 'E' markers) routing throughout the site to connect buildings, pull boxes, transformer pads, and meters. The vision analysis confirmed that underground electric conduit is proposed throughout the site. However, there are no dimension lines or notes showing the clearances from the underground electric conduit to customer buildings, foundations, permanent structures, or other utilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations but provides no coordination dimensions between buildings and proposed underground electric facilities. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general routing of electric lines but provides no evidence that the minimum 60-inch clearance from buildings per UCM § 1.10.5 has been verified or documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires minimum 60-inch (5-foot) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, or permanent structures. The applicant must document this clearance through dimensioned drawings. The existence of underground electric lines on the preliminary electrical plan does not constitute compliance documentation; the clearances must be explicitly shown and dimensioned. The absence of clearance dimensions or notes demonstrating compliance with the 60-inch minimum clearance requirement means the deficiency cannot be marked as resolved. This is a documentation requirement that must be satisfied through additional detail.

findings.comment: No section and plan view exhibit is provided showing utility poles with cross arm dimensions and distances to proposed buildings/structures. Design must provide this exhibit with specific dimensions documenting compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial).
applicableAreas: Clearance verification for proposed buildings near existing utility poles with cross arms
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing distribution poles and overhead utility lines. The poles are shown with cross arm symbols (approximately 8 feet wide for standard distribution poles). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations. However, no section or plan view exhibit is provided that shows the utility poles with cross arms (8 feet width) and dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a 'section and plan view exhibit showing utility poles with cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide) and dimensions from outer conductor to outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.' This exhibit is a fundamental documentation requirement for verifying compliance with the 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance requirements from overhead distribution lines. Without this exhibit, clearance compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: No clearance exhibits are provided showing AE, NESC, and OSHA clearance envelopes in relation to existing overhead facilities and proposed buildings. Exhibits must be provided documenting the clearance envelopes required by applicable standards (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial for distribution; larger for transmission).
applicableAreas: Clearance verification areas where proposed buildings are near overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Existing overhead distribution poles and lines are documented on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey). No clearance exhibits are provided in the site plan set. The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed underground equipment but does not address existing overhead facilities or clearance envelopes.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.10.2 require that clearance exhibits document AE, NESC (National Electrical Safety Code), and OSHA clearance envelopes. These envelopes define the three-dimensional space that must be maintained clear of obstructions around energized conductors for safety. The applicant has not provided any exhibits showing these clearance envelopes in relation to proposed structures. This is a required exhibit that must accompany the site plan when overhead electric facilities are present.

findings.comment: No exhibit is provided with dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing. Design must provide dimensioned drawings showing the distance from each building footprint to the proposed underground electric conduit and lines, demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.5 (minimum 60 inches from customer buildings).
applicableAreas: Proposed underground electric routing between and near proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed underground electric lines (blue lines) routing from the property boundary to four transformer pads and then daisy-chaining to building meter banks. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the building footprints. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings. The relationships shown are purely graphical.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that 'an exhibit be provided showing dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement to verify that proposed underground electric facilities maintain adequate clearances from building foundations (minimum 60 inches per UCM § 1.10.5). Without dimensioned exhibits, the applicant has not demonstrated that the underground routing will comply with clearance standards.

findings.comment: Plan and profile views not submitted to verify required clearances between existing overhead electric lines and proposed buildings. Provide plan and profile cross-sections showing vertical separation between overhead conductors and building structures, with dimensions confirming 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Proposed buildings 1-8 relative to existing overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheets 9, 21, and 31 show the locations of the proposed buildings relative to these overhead facilities in plan view. However, NO PLAN AND PROFILE VIEWS have been provided that show the vertical (profile) relationship between the existing overhead electric lines and the proposed buildings. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires 'Plan and profile not submitted to verify required clearances between existing electric lines and proposed buildings.' The site plan includes plan views showing the buildings and OHE lines, but the profile views (cross-section views showing elevation differences) required to verify clearances are not present in the submittal.
findings.reasoning: Plan view alone is insufficient to verify clearance compliance between overhead conductors and building structures. Profile views (also called cross-sections in plan direction) are required to show the vertical separation between conductor height and building height/roofline. Without these profile views with dimensions, the clearance requirement of 7.5 feet horizontal and 15-foot radial separation cannot be verified. The code specifically requires 'plan and profile' views be submitted. The current submittal contains only plan views for this relationship.

findings.comment: Provide dimensioned underground utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from proposed underground electric conduit to all building foundations and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5. If any location has less than 60 inches, provide alternative routing or written approval from Austin Energy Design.
applicableAreas: Underground electric lines routing to buildings and electrical equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (depicted as solid blue lines) routing from the property boundary through the center of the site, connecting to the four transformer pads and daisy-chaining to building meter banks (located on building walls). Vision analysis found: 'There are no dimensions shown indicating the clearance or offset distance of the underground electrical routing from the building foundations or other structures.' The underground conduit is shown graphically but without dimensional clearances to buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires a minimum 60 inches (5 feet) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer building foundations and permanent structures (except other utilities, which require 12 inches minimum; gas/fuel/steam require 24-36 inches). Without dimensioned drawings showing the distance of the underground lines from building foundations, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with this requirement. This clearance is critical for future excavation safety and building maintenance.
